title: Froezens/Python-Blacklist-Breaker
description: It is an automated Python virtual machine escape payload skipping framework that helps security researchers discover viable payload variants under strict character blacklist restrictions.
llm_applicability_reason: Repository explicitly targets offensive security (exploit development, sandbox bypass) and describes automation (automated payload generation, fuzzing) for security testing.
llm_credibility_reason: Recently updated and description is substantive and clear, but lacks stars and community validation.

title: future-architect/vuls
description: Agent-less vulnerability scanner for Linux, FreeBSD, Container, WordPress, Programming language libraries, Network devices
llm_applicability_reason: Automates vulnerability scanning but does not mention AI, ML, or fuzzing; automation is present but not AI/ML-based as required.
llm_credibility_reason: Very high star count, active maintenance, and substantive description; widely recognized tool.

title: KeygraphHQ/shannon
description: Fully autonomous AI hacker to find actual exploits in your web apps. Shannon has achieved a 96.15% success rate on the hint-free, source-aware XBOW Benchmark.
llm_applicability_reason: The repository explicitly describes itself as a 'fully autonomous AI hacker' for finding exploits in web applications, indicating both offensive security relevance and the use of AI and automation. Topics such as 'penetration-testing' and 'security-automation' further support this.
llm_credibility_reason: The repository has a clear and substantive description, is highly starred (22,666 stars), and was updated recently (2026-02-16), indicating active maintenance and strong community validation. The topics and description suggest it is a serious security tool.
